newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serb leader now ready to sign oath.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb leader now ready to sign oath.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb leader who boycotted the inaugural meeting of the Bosnian Presidency this weekend said on Tuesday that he was ready to reverse his stand and take part in the work of joint governing bodies.

Momcilo Krajisnik said after meeting the German ambassador to Sarajevo, Johannes Preisinger, that if other members of the parliament were in agreement, the oath could be signed at a new ceremony, Bosnian Serb Television reported.
Krajisnik is the Serb member of the newly-elected Bosnian Presidency which is led by Alija Izetbegovic, a Moslem, and also includes Kresimir Zubak, a Croat.

The United States said on Monday it was "furious" over the Bosnian Serbs' boycott of the first session of Bosnia's peacetime parliament, and threatened new sanctions unless they complied with the Dayton peace accords.

Foreign dignitaries, including U.S. envoy John Kornblum, waited for more than three hours on Saturday for Serb representatives to appear at the ceremony in Sarajevo, but they failed to show up, claiming security concerns.
Krajisnik said the Bosnian Serbs' non-attendance at Saturday's session had been politicized with the aim of blaming the Serbs for not wanting to work in joint institutions.

"Our position is: we wish to work in the joint institutions, and we reject all accusations that we obstructed the work of the (inaugural) session," he said, adding that the Bosnian Serbs had put forward several compromise solutions.
"That misunderstanding has aggravated an already politicized situation which does not lead to rapprochement, but rather is aimed at laying the blame on our side," Krajisnik said.

Despite this, he said he was ready to recommend to his deputies to sign the oath "so that... we make a contribution and take an active step towards continuing the process of setting up joint institutions."
Krajisnik added that he wanted the ceremony to be held on Bosnian Serb territory, an event unlikely to happen after the Serb snub on Saturday.
